title: Multiplayer Cell Division Animation
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D educational animation of cell division (mitosis) using Three.js. Load the 'MosquitoInAmber.glb' model using GLTFLoader as a preserved specimen reference object displayed in the corner of the scene.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a dark blue background (0x0a0a2e) to simulate a microscope view.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and two directional lights (one white from above at intensity 0.8, one blue-tinted from below at intensity 0.3).
- Camera starts at position (0, 5, 12) looking at origin.
- OrbitControls enabled for camera rotation.
- Load 'MosquitoInAmber.glb' and place it at position (-6, 0, -4) scaled to 0.5. This serves as the 'preserved specimen' reference in the lab.

CELL DIVISION SIMULATION:
- Create a 'parent cell' as a semi-transparent sphere (radius 1.5, color 0x44cc88, opacity 0.6) at the origin.
- Inside the parent cell, create 4 small spheres representing chromosomes (radius 0.15, color 0xff4444), initially clustered at center.
- The simulation has 6 phases: INTERPHASE, PROPHASE, METAPHASE, ANAPHASE, TELOPHASE, CYTOKINESIS.
- Each phase lasts 3 seconds when playing.

PHASE BEHAVIORS:
- INTERPHASE: Cell is round, chromosomes scattered randomly inside. Cell scale = 1.0.
- PROPHASE: Chromosomes move toward center, cell slightly enlarges (scale 1.1). Chromosomes become 8 (duplicated).
- METAPHASE: 8 chromosomes align along the X=0 plane (equator). Cell scale = 1.15.
- ANAPHASE: Chromosomes split into two groups of 4, moving to opposite poles (x = -1.0 and x = 1.0). Cell elongates on X axis (scaleX = 1.5, scaleY = 0.85).
- TELOPHASE: Cell pinches in the middle (create a visible pinch using a torus or deformation). Two nuclear envelopes form (small transparent spheres around each chromosome group).
- CYTOKINESIS: Cell splits into two daughter cells, each with 4 chromosomes. Daughter cells move apart to x = -2.5 and x = 2.5. Each daughter cell has radius 1.0.

MULTIPLAYER FEATURE:
- Support two 'players' who can each control a cell. Player 1 uses WASD keys, Player 2 uses Arrow keys.
- After CYTOKINESIS completes, Player 1 controls the left daughter cell, Player 2 controls the right daughter cell.
- Players can move their cells in the XZ plane within bounds [-8, 8].
- Each player has a score that increments by 1 each time they press their 'action' key (Player 1: Space, Player 2: Enter) which triggers their cell to undergo another division cycle (only if not already dividing).

HUD / UI:
- Display current phase name in a top-center div (id='phase-label', font-size 24px, white text).
- 'Play/Pause' button (id='btn-play-pause') toggles animation.
- 'Reset' button (id='btn-reset') resets everything to INTERPHASE with one parent cell.
- 'Speed' slider (id='slider-speed', range 0.5 to 3.0, step 0.1, default 1.0) controls animation speed multiplier.
- Player 1 score display (id='p1-score') and Player 2 score display (id='p2-score').
- Phase progress bar (id='progress-bar') showing percentage through current phase (0-100).

STATE MANAGEMENT (window.__3D_STATE__):
- currentPhase: string (one of 'INTERPHASE','PROPHASE','METAPHASE','ANAPHASE','TELOPHASE','CYTOKINESIS','COMPLETE')
- phaseIndex: number 0-6
- isPlaying: boolean
- speedMultiplier: number
- phaseProgress: number 0-100
- chromosomeCount: number (total visible chromosomes)
- parentCellScale: {x, y, z} of the parent cell
- daughterCellsExist: boolean
- daughterCellPositions: [{x,y,z}, {x,y,z}] or null
- p1Score: number
- p2Score: number
- p1CellPosition: {x, y, z} or null
- p2CellPosition: {x, y, z} or null
- modelLoaded: boolean (true when MosquitoInAmber.glb loaded)
- totalCells: number (count of all cells in scene)
- animationTime: number (elapsed time in seconds)
- boundaryEnforced: boolean (true if movement bounds are active)
physics_constraints: Cells must remain within [-8, 8] bounds on X and Z axes. Chromosome positions must remain inside their parent cell boundaries. Daughter cells after cytokinesis must have equal chromosome counts (conservation of genetic material). Cell volumes should approximately conserve during division (parent volume ≈ 2 × daughter volume). Animation timing must scale linearly with speed multiplier. No NaN values in any position or scale properties.
